My plot is very small, only 0.06 hectares, and I plant my cassava and cocoyam together with some vegetables like I always do. I cannot afford to buy fertilizer from the agro-dealer this year, but I will carry the waste from my goats and kitchen ash to spread on the mounds like my mother taught me. I will use the cassava stems I cut from last year's harvest — they grow well enough for my family's pot, and the rain here in the South East is plenty so I do not need to fetch water for the plot. My children help me on weekends, but most of the weeding and heaping I do myself with my hoe.
